## Overview

This meta-analysis (PMID 24315724; DOI 10.1016/S0140-6736(13)62343-0) searched Medline from Jan 1, 2009, to Nov 19, 2013 for phase 3 randomised trials of patients with atrial fibrillation randomised to new oral anticoagulants or [warfarin](./warfarin.md) and reporting both efficacy and safety outcomes. It pooled all 71,683 participants from the RE-LY, ROCKET AF, ARISTOTLE and ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48 trials, of whom 42,411 received a new oral anticoagulant and 29,272 received warfarin, using a random-effects model ([src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63.md)).

## Reported findings

New oral anticoagulants reduced stroke or systemic embolic events by 19% versus warfarin (RR 0.81, 95% CI 0.73-0.91; p<0.0001), mainly driven by a reduction in haemorrhagic stroke (0.49, 0.38-0.64; p<0.0001), and also reduced all-cause mortality (0.90, 0.85-0.95; p=0.0003) and intracranial haemorrhage (0.48, 0.39-0.59; p<0.0001), but increased gastrointestinal bleeding (1.25, 1.01-1.55; p=0.04). Low-dose regimens showed similar overall reductions in stroke or systemic embolic events to warfarin (1.03, 0.84-1.27; p=0.74) with a more favourable bleeding profile (0.65, 0.43-1.00; p=0.05) but significantly more ischaemic strokes (1.28, 1.02-1.60; p=0.045) ([src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63.md)).

The greater relative reduction in major bleeding with new oral anticoagulants was observed when centre-based time in therapeutic range was less than 66% (0.69, 0.59-0.81) than when it was 66% or more (0.93, 0.76-1.13; p for interaction 0.022) ([src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63.md)).
